issues.detail: The Greek 'μηδεποτε... ελθειν δυναμενα' means 'never able to come/reach,' but the Vietnamese 'chẳng bao giờ có thể đến được' is missing the grammatical dependency on the preceding action. More importantly, the Greek structure implies a continuous state of 'being unable' while learning; the Vietnamese phrasing slightly obscures the fact that 'dynamena' (able) modifies the ability to reach the knowledge, not just the act of reaching it.
